paragraphs: Swamiji had little patience for religion done like a drill: kneeling at a fixed time, standing at ease, repeating words mechanically while the mind wanders off elsewhere. That, he said, has nothing to do with real religion. To make the point he told a story about Guru Nanak, the great prophet who founded the Sikh faith about four hundred years earlier.

One day Guru Nanak walked into a large mosque where the faithful were lined up for prayer, kneeling and rising together and repeating the same words after the mullah who led them. As the mullah called on the most merciful and kind God, the teacher of all teachers, Guru Nanak began to smile and remarked that the man was a hypocrite.
The mullah flew into a rage and demanded to know why he was smiling. Because you are not praying at all, Guru Nanak replied calmly. There is no prayer in you.

Furious, the mullah went to the magistrate. This unbeliever had come into their mosque and laughed at them during prayers, he complained, and the only fitting punishment was death. Guru Nanak was brought in and asked to explain himself. He said he smiled because the man had not been praying. If the mullah were called, he added, he would show what the mullah had really been doing. The mullah was summoned, and Guru Nanak asked that he be given the Koran to swear on. Then he revealed it: all the while the mullah's lips were saying "Allah, Allah," his mind was on a chicken he had left at home.

The mullah was stunned. He was a little more honest than most, so he admitted it was true. Guru Nanak was set free, and the magistrate gave the mullah some advice: it is better to stay away from the mosque altogether than to go there and pretend. Don't pray when your heart isn't in it, and don't call on God while thinking about your chicken.
learn: Going through the motions, whether in prayer, in class or in a conversation, is not the same as being present. Wherever you are, try to have your mind and your body in the same place. One honest minute counts for more than an hour of empty routine.
